title: Schedule of Hold, Discharge and Closing Settings, Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services
content:
Plans of care under **Outpatient and Part B Therapy Services** carry the following hold, discharge and closing settings in every tier.

| Tier | Plan put on hold while the resident is hospitalized | Days a plan may stay on hold before it is discharged and a new evaluation is needed | Resident may decline further therapy and have the plan discharged | Resident discharged from therapy referred to the restorative nursing program at no charge | Discharged plan closed only with a zero balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicare Part B Physical Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Medicare Part B Occupational Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Medicare Part B Speech-Language Pathology Plan of Care | Yes | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Medicare Advantage Outpatient Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Medical Assistance Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Private Pay Therapy Plan of Care | Yes | 30 | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Settings restated

- **Hold.** A plan is put on hold while the resident is hospitalized, and may stay on hold for 30 days. A plan on hold longer than that is discharged, and a new evaluation is needed.
- **Declining therapy.** The resident may decline further therapy and have the plan discharged.
- **Restorative nursing.** A resident discharged from therapy is referred to the restorative nursing program at no charge.
- **Closing.** A discharged plan is closed only with a zero balance.

## Hypothetical illustrations

| Hypothetical plan | Reading |
|---|---|
| On hold for 19 days, resident returns | Within the 30 days |
| On hold for 41 days | Past the 30 days: discharged, and a new evaluation is needed |
| Discharged plan with $12.65 still owed | Not closed while a balance remains |
